strategy.name: Breakout_ATR_XAU_USTEC_1h
strategy.rationale: 20-bar breakout on cheapest-spread markets, ATR volatility confirms real move, RSI avoids exhausted extremes. Wide TP vs tight SL fixes inverted R:R that destroyed v8.

history.analysis: 28% WR with 1:3 TP:SL ratio inverted—avg win $9.47 vs avg loss $12.02 means R:R is actually negative. Nearly all profit from time-exits, stops destroying equity. SMA crossover entries too late, choppy markets causing whipsaws.
mistakes: R:R inverted: TP 1.2% but avg win only $9.47 vs avg loss $12.02—stops hit before targets, net negative even ignoring WR
SMA cross is a lagging entry—by signal candle, move largely complete, stop within noise range gets clipped immediately
EURJPY spread 0.033% eats edge on 1h moves; two recent EURJPY trades both losers with spread cost ~$1.54 each
maxHoldMinutes 1200 (20h) forces time-exits at tiny wins while stops run full 0.4%—asymmetric truncation of winners
changes: Switch to breakout-based entries on clean N-bar highs/lows to reduce lag versus SMA cross
Fix R:R: TP must be at least 2x SL in pct terms, and widen TP relative to stop to let winners run
Focus on XAU and USTEC exclusively—cheapest spreads, best edge retention
Add ATR filter to avoid entering in low-volatility chop where stops get clipped
Add session filter to avoid illiquid hours where spreads widen and fakeouts increase

strategy.name: Breakout_ATR_XAU_USTEC_1h
strategy.rationale: 20-bar breakout on cheapest-spread markets, ATR volatility confirms real move, RSI avoids exhausted extremes. Wide TP vs tight SL fixes inverted R:R that destroyed v8.

history.analysis: 30% WR with 1:2.5 R:R needs ~40% to break even. Stops hit hard (-$158), time exits profit slightly. Spread costs manageable. Core issue: low win rate from poor entry timing and trading counter-momentum on noisy 1h crosses.
mistakes: Win rate far too low for the R:R ratio - need ~40% WR minimum for 1:2.5 to be profitable, achieving only 30%
SMA cross entries lag significantly on 1h, entering after move already exhausted - evidenced by immediate stop-outs
USTEC shorts repeatedly stopped out quickly (3 losses in a row), suggesting counter-trend entries against strong bull trend
EURJPY and EURAUD trades show spread eating time-exit profits - EURAUD 0.16% round-trip destroys small wins
changes: Drop EURAUD and AUDJPY - spreads too expensive relative to move size for this account
Focus on XAU and USTEC - cheapest spreads, allow larger R:R targets
Require breakout confirmation before SMA cross entry to reduce lag
Tighten session to NY/London overlap for XAU where volume is highest
Increase R:R to 1:3 minimum to make low WR viable, or increase WR via stricter filters

strategy.name: TrendFollow_SMABreak_1h_EURJPY_XAU
strategy.rationale: SMA cross only when price already beyond SMA50 AND momentum confirms, plus RSI not overbought at entry. Triple-filter reduces false crosses that caused most losses.

history.analysis: 28.6% WR with PF 0.38 is catastrophic. Mean-reversion fighting strong trends. 72% of losses are stops hit, not timeouts. Counter-trend entries on trending instruments. R:R 2:1 theoretical but actual wins tiny vs losses.
mistakes: Counter-trend mean-reversion against persistent macro trends in XAU and USTEC - both in strong directional moves
15m timeframe too noisy for Bollinger reversion; price tags band then continues, stop hit before bounce
USTEC shorts repeatedly stopped out during uptrend - no trend filter applied before fading extremes
Early versions traded BTC, AUDJPY, EURAUD with expensive spreads and tiny moves - spread consumed edge
changes: Switch to trend-following to align with dominant market direction
Add higher-timeframe SMA filter to prohibit counter-trend trades
Focus on XAU and USTEC only for cheap spreads; drop crypto and exotic FX
Use 1h timeframe for cleaner signals and larger moves relative to spread
Require momentum confirmation before entry, not just band touch

strategy.name: SMACross_Momentum_1h_XAU_EURJPY
strategy.rationale: SMA cross with momentum filter on trending instruments. EURJPY trends well intraday; XAU ultra-cheap. Higher timeframe avoids noise. No counter-trend trades ever. Moderate R:R 1:2.5 with trend alignment.

history.analysis: 27.8% WR with 1:2.5 R:R needs ~40% WR to break even. Breakouts failing repeatedly—price reverses after entry. Spread costs manageable; problem is signal quality and stop placement.
mistakes: Breakout entries on 15m are chasing—price exhausted at N-bar highs/lows, reversing immediately into stops
0.7% stop too tight for USTEC 15m ATR; stops hit before trend develops, as shown by 4 consecutive USTEC stop-outs
BTC entries (v1) had no trend filter and expensive spread—all 3 trades stopped out quickly
AUDJPY entry ignored spread cost relative to expected move; 0.033% round-trip on tight stop = edge destruction
changes: Abandon pure breakout entries; switch to pullback/mean-reversion or confirmed-momentum approaches
Use wider stops sized to actual ATR multiples, reduce position sizing to compensate
Restrict to XAU and USTEC only for lowest spread cost; remove BTC/ETH/SOL/FX from all strategies

strategy.name: BollingerReversion_15m_XAU
strategy.rationale: Mean-reversion on Bollinger extremes with RSI confirmation. XAU ultra-cheap spread. Counter-trend but high-frequency signals improve sample size quickly.

history.analysis: 29% WR, PF 0.43: strategy trades against momentum, stops hit constantly. Mean reversion without trend filter loses repeatedly. Time exits capture small wins; stops take large losses. Spread costs minor vs directional losses.
mistakes: Trading mean reversion against strong trends - most stops are momentum continuation moves crushing counter-trend entries
No trend filter: entering longs/shorts purely on RSI+BB without confirming macro direction leads to catching falling/rising knives
USTEC shorts during uptrend (28449,28582,29124,29173 all losing) - systematic directional blindness
BTC entries with 0.02% spread manageable but 1h stop too tight for BTC volatility - all 3 BTC trades stopped out immediately
changes: Switch to trend-following breakouts to align with momentum instead of fighting it
Use SMA cross trend filter as primary signal, only trade in direction of trend
Focus on USTEC and XAU (lowest spreads) where edge-to-cost ratio is best
Widen TP relative to SL for genuine asymmetry, reduce hold time to avoid overnight gaps on FX/XAU

strategy.name: VolatilityBreakout_15m_USTEC_XAU
strategy.rationale: 15m breakout of 30-bar high/low during active session with ATR filter ensures sufficient move size. Higher trade frequency on cheapest-spread instruments improves statistical sample quickly.

history.analysis: WR 27%, PF 0.30: system is bleeding. Most losses are stop-outs, not time exits. Mean reversion firing into strong trends. USTEC/XAU now deeply oversold - momentum still negative, wrong to fade yet. 73h idle suggests conditions too strict or weekend closure.
mistakes: Fading momentum into trending moves: USTEC shorted at 28449 then 28582 while in downtrend - mean reversion against trend is dangerous
Stop too tight at 1.1% on 1h causing frequent stop-outs (8 of 15 trades stopped out); reward rarely reached before reversal
Trading EURAUD and AUDJPY with 0.16-0.033% spread eats edge on small moves; spread cost disproportionate to avg win
No trend filter: entering longs/shorts purely on RSI/BB without confirming broader direction led to catching falling knives
changes: Add trend filter (price_vs_sma 50) to only trade mean reversion in direction of higher-timeframe trend
Widen stops to 1.5-1.8% to survive noise, compensate with larger R:R target 3R
Remove expensive spread markets (ETH, SOL, EURAUD) from mean reversion; keep USTEC and XAU only
Relax entry: drop momentum filter or loosen threshold - it was blocking valid oversold entries
Extend maxHoldMinutes to 1440 (24h) so winners have time to develop

strategy.name: TrendAligned_MeanReversion_1h_USTEC_XAU
strategy.rationale: Mean reversion only when price vs SMA50 aligns with oversold/overbought RSI below 30 or above 70, widened stops reduce false stops, extended hold allows targets to develop.

history.analysis: 26.7% WR with 1:1.1 R:R is fatal—need >47% WR minimum. 11/15 losses, mostly stops. Time-exits slightly better than stops. 15m noise generating false signals; spread cost manageable but entries poor.
mistakes: R:R of 1:1.1 requires >47% WR to break even; achieved only 26.7% — mathematically doomed
15m timeframe too noisy: SMA crosses whipsaw repeatedly, especially USTEC short signals hit stops within 45-75m
BTC included in v1 despite highest spread cost relative to move size; three consecutive BTC losses
AUDJPY has expensive spread (0.033%) and small pip moves on 15m — spread consumes edge
changes: Move to 1h timeframe to reduce noise and improve signal quality
Increase R:R to minimum 1:2 to be profitable at lower WR
Restrict to cheapest-spread markets only: USTEC, XAU
Widen stops to 1.0-1.2% to survive normal ATR noise
Add ATR volatility filter to avoid entering in compression

strategy.name: RSI_Mean_Reversion_1h_Gold_Nasdaq
strategy.rationale: Fade extremes on cheapest markets: RSI oversold/overbought with Bollinger band touch. Mean reversion on liquid instruments; 2R target, stops below band extreme, fewer but higher-quality signals.

history.analysis: 7/7 stops hit, 0 winners. Stop 0.4% too tight for 1h volatility; trailing stop 0.25% prematurely exits; RSI pullback entries catch falling knives; BTC overtraded (3 losses); AUDJPY spread erodes edge.
mistakes: Stop 0.4% far too tight for 1h candles on BTC/XAU/USTEC - normal noise exceeds it, causing immediate stop-outs
Trailing stop 0.25% triggers before any meaningful move develops, locking in losses on winners
RSI<45 pullback in uptrend often means trend is actually reversing, not a healthy dip
BTC traded 3 times with expensive 0.02% spread and wide ATR - cost/volatility ratio unfavorable at 1h
changes: Widen stop to match instrument ATR; target 2R minimum so spread cost is <10% of risk
Remove trailing stop or widen significantly to let trades breathe
Replace RSI pullback with breakout/momentum confirmation to avoid catching knives
Drop BTC; focus on USTEC and XAU (cheapest spreads) plus low-spread FX
Add session filter to trade only high-liquidity hours

strategy.name: DualMA_Trend_15m_Indices
strategy.rationale: 15m dual SMA cross with RSI trend confirmation. Faster timeframe gives more trades with defined momentum; stops sized to 15m ATR range; cheapest spreads dominate allocation.
